title: Animation / Classic principles

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; visible default tab states

slide_intent: Adapt familiar animation principles to a brand’s intended behavior so movement remains understandable and consistent with its character.
strategic_value: Restrained geometric demonstrations can give IBM a precise motion vocabulary while retaining enough surprise to engage viewers.
demonstration: The webpage presents twelve animation principles in order, each with explanatory copy and a green/red pair of captured demonstration frames.
practical_value: Use the paired guidance to decide how timing, staging, overlap and deformation should express IBM’s controlled motion character.

content_islands.name: Opening interpretation
content_islands.spec: Begin with the note that IBM interprets the twelve classic animation principles for graphic forms.

content_islands.name: Action and staging
content_islands.spec: Group Squash and stretch, Anticipation and Staging with their paired blue-and-pink geometric demonstrations.

content_islands.name: Poses and transitions
content_islands.spec: Continue with Pose to pose, Overlapping action, Slow in and slow out, and Arc; preserve their sequential reading order and paired evaluations.

content_islands.name: Support and timing
content_islands.spec: Follow with Secondary action, Timing and Exaggeration, keeping the short behavioral rationale attached to each pair.

content_islands.name: Weight and appeal
content_islands.spec: End with Solid drawing and Appeal before the page navigation; the capture preserves only individual demonstration states.

reference_purposes.Intent: The introduction explains adapting character-animation principles to graphic forms; Staging explicitly connects sequence and restraint to directing attention.
reference_purposes.Application: The source supplies guidance on key poses, overlapping motion, timing, axes, weight and secondary action.
reference_purposes.Constraint: It discourages overt deformation, bouncing curves, abrupt stops and long exponential settling; secondary action must support rather than distract from the main action.
